Issued at 212 PM EDT Wed Oct 28 2026

===== Pleasant Weather Lingers with Increasing Clouds Halloween =====

Ridge of high pressure centered over the Eastern Conus and Northeast 
will continue to heavily influence our weather conditions for the 
next few days. This afternoon highs should top out in the mid to 
upper 70s with any remnant clouds clearing. After sunset this 
evening, skies will remain clear as low temperatures will fall near 
where they were this morning, in the mid 40s to low 50s. Patchy 
river fog is possible again in the morning, so those driving in the 
deepest river valleys used to seeing this should continue to take 
care while driving in this persistent, early-morning, and patchy 
valley fog.

Tomorrow, SW flow surges a little stronger ahead of a slowing cold 
front that will approach our area from the NNW. Tomorrow's weather 
won't be much different than today, in fact maybe a touch warmer 
with highs in the upper 70s and isolated 80s, especially in far 
southwest and western communities. Clear skies tomorrow morning will 
begin to cloud over some with high level cirrus streaming in from 
disturbance that will affect Texas and New Mexico. Otherwise, we are 
dry and warmer than average. The aforementioned cold front will 
slowly sag towards our southern Indiana counties in the evening and 
overnight hours on Thursday into Friday. 

Here, there begins discrepancies between short range model 
solutions. This cold front will very slowly trudge through Indiana 
and eventually Kentucky through the day on Friday. Even though it is 
rather slow, it will be aided by a weak high pressure that will try 
to build from the surface and up to 850 mb or so in our west over 
Missouri. Combined with the clockwise rotation, there'll be a subtle 
push of cooler air into our area with northerly winds. How quickly 
this occurs could drop our highs from their current forecast from 
the mid 70s to mid 60s and low 70s on Friday. The later the time, 
the warmer the highs. Clouds will increase during the day and will 
lower in height, further limiting warming during the day from that 
disturbance over Texas.

By Halloween, cloudy skies stay put over the entire area as 
temperatures remain mild near the low 70s. A pattern shift is in 
store this weekend as the original high over the Northeast moves 
away and another high from Canada tries to build in. Simultaneously, 
a stalled boundary along the Gulf Coast may have enough energy to 
form another low there that could push moisture into our area, 
although trends have hampered its development. Should a low form, in 
combination with the weakening ridge, there may be enough of a 
window of opportunity to surge moisture north into KY. This all 
depends on the strength and timing of the interaction of the rain 
with the advancing high. Should the low form too far south near FL, 
we may actually remain dry Sunday, or just have spotty showers. For 
now, PoPs have been lowered into the 40-50% range, with anywhere 
from a trace to as much as 0.5" possible (75% of remaining below 
0.5"), with the heaviest totals across the south and lighter heading 
north. It should be noted that rainfall totals on Sunday are left-
skewed towards remaining dry according to RRFS data. Good news is 
trick-or-treating activities will remain dry on Saturday night!

===== Busy Weather Pattern Next Week =====

Beyond Sunday, spotty showers may remain as southerly flow remains 
in place with brief ridging on Monday. A substantial trough will be 
moving through the country, possibly creating a cut-off low that 
will meander through the southern Plains. However close this gets to 
our area will depend on how much the jet over Canada can steer the 
low towards KY. Should the jet remain too far north, our next rain 
chances will be delayed beyond Wednesday. If the cut-off low can 
remain far enough north, then a good amount of widespread is 
possible earlier on Wednesday, lasting through Thursday or Friday. 
On average, additional rainfall totals range near 0.75-1.25", though 
this depends on the factors mentioned before. Temperatures will 
remain near the low 70s or cooler on potentially rainier days like 
on Wednesday.
